clue.text: Separate Easter egg roughly

indicators.note: done roughly means done without care for order, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the two words supply the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaks apart a chocolate Easter egg without much care.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to set apart or keep in distinct groups, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Audibly recognise certain beach

indicators.note: something done audibly is heard rather than read, so the words that follow are judged by their sound

blocks.note: to recognise is to see, and certain is sure; said together they match a two-part word for the coast

explanation.surface: Someone claims they could pick out a particular beach just by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The seashore is the strip of land beside the sea, which is what a beach is.

clue.text: Dark brush changing hands

indicators.note: the hands are right and left, so one hand's letter is swapped for the other's

blocks.note: to brush a horse is to groom it

explanation.surface: A brush passes from one owner to another, perhaps a sale in a dim shop.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) and L (left) are the two hands: in GROOM the R becomes an L, giving GLOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is darkness or murky shade, so the noun sense of dark (as in 'after dark') fits.

clue.text: Doctor Bear felt intern to be a brat

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a fresh order

blocks.note: the three words supply all fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital doctor named Bear thinks a junior intern is behaving like a spoilt child.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally 'terrible child', describes an unruly or shocking young person, so a brat.

clue.text: Weak US intelligence service maintaining average returns

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so the agency's letters hold another word inside them
something that returns goes back the way it came, so the whole result is read backwards

blocks.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
the mean is an average

explanation.surface: A feeble American spy agency keeps coming back with mediocre results.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic figuratively means lacking vigour or strength, from the pale, tired look of blood deficiency.

clue.text: Account for old grassland

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a plain is a wide flat grassy area

explanation.surface: Someone asked to justify an old meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give a reason or description that makes it understood.

clue.text: Escape without love that's keen

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for love is taken away

blocks.note: to avoid is to escape or evade
love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An eager person runs away from love.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid describes someone eager and enthusiastic, as in an avid reader.

clue.text: Bitter civil riot erupting

indicators.note: an eruption throws things about violently, so these letters land in new places

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Resentment boils over into a riot among the citizenry.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic speech is caustic and full of acid hostility, so harshly bitter.

clue.text: Detectives have the ability to alarm

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
may expresses being able or permitted to do something

explanation.surface: Police detectives are capable of frightening people.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to fill them with consternation or sudden worry, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Blameless bachelor pair dancing round about

indicators.note: dancers move about the floor, so these letters move into a new arrangement
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go either side of another short word

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged
re is Latin for 'concerning', used in memos

explanation.surface: A single man and his partner waltz around innocently.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreproachable means beyond criticism or fault, so free of any blame.

clue.text: Reserved area idiot rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for idiot is read backwards

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
a fool is an idiot

explanation.surface: A booked area has been turned down by a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person keeps their distance and is cool or detached in manner.

clue.text: Equipment program a traitor bugs regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
taken as written
a rat is a betrayer
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A spy's kit: software that a turncoat uses to plant listening bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the set of tools or machinery needed for a task, a collective synonym.

clue.text: Strange hymn about leaders of old men's organisation — it sounds the same

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters appear in an unusual order
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the selected ones
leaders go in front, so the first letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged
the initial letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An odd hymn is sung by an elderly men's club, and it never varies.
explanation.definitionFit: A homonym is a word with the same pronunciation or spelling as another but a different meaning.

clue.text: Old lady returning with Heather into country

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for old lady is read right to left

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's 'old lady'
Erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: Mum travels home with her friend Heather into another country.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather is capitalised to look like a name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: America, as the United States is commonly called, is a nation.

clue.text: Run after distant TV director?

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the word for run is placed second, behind the word for distant

blocks.note: remote means far away
to run a business is to control it

explanation.surface: Chasing down a television director who is aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the word for run comes second. 'TV director' sounds like a person who directs programmes; the question mark flags the gadget instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The handheld device directs a television from across the room, changing channels and volume, so whimsically a director.

clue.text: Process of setter having tea with revolting wrong man

indicators.note: revolting is read as turning over, so the word for wrong is flipped round

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a sin is a wrong
M is the abbreviation for man

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler describes taking tea with a disgusting, wicked man.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanism is the working process or system by which something happens, as in a defence mechanism.

clue.text: Cut off from line of hills below Eastern Way

indicators.note: in a down answer below means lower in the column, so the hills come after the direction and road

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
St (street) is a way
a range is a chain of hills or mountains

explanation.surface: A route is cut off from the hills below an eastern road.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'below' puts the hills after E and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, separating someone from people they were close to.

clue.text: Facts show boxing master's position

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so the show's letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: a circus is a travelling show
M is an abbreviation for master, as in an MA (Master of Arts)
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Evidence from a show reveals where a boxing champion stood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport; it means enclosing. The possessive on master just joins it to position.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumstances are the conditions and facts surrounding an event, as in 'given the circumstances'.

clue.text: Improve on high graduate gets with drug

blocks.note: up means high above
grad is the short form of graduate
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A graduate who is high gets better with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrade something is to raise it to a better standard or level.

clue.text: Dog Zeus initially hides in his hut, unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things not as you would predict, so the letters appear rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the god's name is kept
something that hides in a place goes inside it, so that letter sits within the others

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A dog named Zeus surprises everyone by hiding inside its owner's hut.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shih Tzu is a small long-haired toy breed originally from Tibet and China.

clue.text: Religious leader with time to talk and talk

blocks.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rabbi has time to chat at length.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit means to chatter at tedious length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'.

clue.text: In the morning, tiny bit of amanatsu zest is fantastic

indicators.note: a tiny bit of a word is just its first letter

blocks.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon
the opening letter of the fruit's name
zing is liveliness or zest

explanation.surface: A breakfast tip: a sprinkle of citrus peel from a Japanese amanatsu fruit is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Zest looks like the peel of the citrus; it is the energy sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something remarkable that astonishes or delights, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Puffer at home gets healthier

blocks.note: someone at home is in
hale means healthy, so haler is healthier

explanation.surface: A smoker who stays home grows healthier.
explanation.definitionFit: An asthma sufferer's device is puffed to deliver medicine, so it is nicknamed a puffer.

clue.text: Perhaps Caterpillar tractor's rear trapped in rock

indicators.note: the rear is the back end, so only the final letter of the vehicle is kept
something trapped in is held inside, so that letter goes into the rock

blocks.note: lava is molten rock that cools into stone
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The back of a Caterpillar tractor is stuck in a rock fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Caterpillar is a brand of heavy machinery, which fits tractor; split off, it is a grub. 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the immature, feeding stage of a butterfly or moth, one example of an insect grub.

clue.text: Sparkling brook Scotsman found in Bute, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first and third
found in means located inside, so the stream and the man sit within the island's letters

blocks.note: the first and third letters
a rill is a small stream
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A sparkling stream and a Scot are discovered on the Isle of Bute.
explanation.walkthrough: Bute is an island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means shining brightly, as a gem sparkles with light.

clue.text: Obstacle regarding title

blocks.note: a bar is a barrier
on means about, as in 'a book on birds'

explanation.surface: A legal hurdle concerning a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a rank of nobility, a hereditary or life title in the peerage.

clue.text: Sent a message about pet

definitions.note: adjective, as in a pet rabbit

indicators.note: about here means carried around inside, so the answer is concealed within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and through the next two

explanation.surface: Someone texted about their pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet animal is domesticated and docile, living with people rather than wild.

clue.text: European, having arithmetical facility to make a list

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
numerate means competent with numbers

explanation.surface: A European good at sums draws up a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to name items one by one, which is how you compile a list.
